2027-04-29.title: Saint Catherine of Siena, Virgin and Doctor of the Church
readings: God has made no distinction between them and us, cleansing their hearts by faith
Proclaim his marvellous deeds to all the nations (or: Alleluia)
Abide in my love, so that my joy may be in you, and that your joy may be complete
2027-04-29.alt: Memorial. Thursday of the Fifth Week of Easter (Year I). The weekday readings are given here; the proper readings of the memorial, 1 John 1:5–2:2 and Matthew 11:25–30, may be used instead. St Catherine is a patron of Italy and of Europe. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-04-29.verse: As the Father has loved me, so I have loved you; abide in my love.
theo: The council in Jerusalem reaches its decision. “After there had been much debate, Peter stood up.” He reminds the assembly that God chose him to bring the Gospel to the Gentiles in the house of Cornelius, and that God “who knows the human heart, testified to them by giving them the Holy Spirit, just as he did to us; and in cleansing their hearts by faith he has made no distinction between them and us.” Then comes the sentence that sums up the whole matter: “we believe that we will be saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, just as they will.” Salvation is not earned by keeping a list of customs; it is a gift received in faith, for Jew and Gentile alike. The assembly falls silent and listens to Barnabas and Paul tell of the signs God has worked among the nations. Then James, the leader of the church in Jerusalem, speaks. He reads the prophet Amos, “I will rebuild the dwelling of David, which has fallen,” so that “all other peoples may seek the Lord,” and gives his judgment: “we should not trouble those Gentiles who are turning to God,” asking only a few things that would let Jewish and Gentile believers share one table in peace. Peter speaks first, James confirms, the whole assembly listens: this is how the Church discerns. James also honours the Law of Moses, “read aloud every sabbath in the synagogues”; the decision does not despise Israel's heritage but opens its promises to all.

In the Gospel Jesus tells us where the grace that saves us comes from: “As the Father has loved me, so I have loved you; abide in my love.” The love between the Father and the Son is poured out on the disciples, and the commandments are simply the way to stay in it. And the goal is joy: “I have said these things to you so that my joy may be in you, and that your joy may be complete.” Few saints show this joy on fire more clearly than St Catherine of Siena (1347 to 1380). The twenty-third or twenty-fourth child of a dyer in Siena, she joined the Dominican lay women called the Mantellate, nursed the sick through plague, made peace between feuding families and cities, and, though she had little schooling, dictated The Dialogue and hundreds of letters. She loved the Church so much that she wrote to the Pope as “sweet Christ on earth,” and she also told him plainly to return from Avignon to Rome, which Gregory XI did in 1377. She died in Rome on 29 April 1380, aged thirty-three. Paul VI named her a Doctor of the Church in 1970. She wrote to a disciple (in substance): if you are what you ought to be, you will set the whole of Italy on fire. And she prayed (in substance): eternal Trinity, you are a deep sea; the more I enter, the more I find, and the more I find, the more I seek you.
outline: Ask: is your faith a burden you carry or a love you live in?
Peter's word at the council: no distinction between them and us.
The Father's love for the Son poured out on us.
Point 3 · Set the world on fire
St Catherine: joy, truth and love for the Church.
live: Receive grace, do not earn it (Acts 15:11)
Make an act of thanksgiving today for one gift you know you did not deserve.
Speak the truth in love, like Catherine
Say one honest and kind word today that you have been avoiding, and pray for the Pope and the bishops.
2027-04-29.prayer: Father, as you have loved your Son, so he has loved us; keep us in his love. You set St Catherine of Siena on fire with love for Christ crucified and for his Church: grant that, through her prayers, we may be saved by the grace of the Lord Jesus, speak the truth with courage and charity, and find in your love the joy that is complete. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen.
altar: St Catherine's confessor and biographer, Blessed Raymond of Capua, records that for long periods she could take almost no food except Holy Communion. She lived from the altar. The Eucharist is the love of the Father and the Son given to us as food, so that we may abide in that love.

quick: At the council in Jerusalem Peter declared that Jews and Gentiles alike are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus.
James confirmed it, and the Church decided not to burden Gentile believers with the whole Law of Moses.
Jesus asks us to abide in his love so that his joy may be in us; St Catherine of Siena lived that love with fire.
2027-04-29.action: Pray today for the Pope and for the unity of the Church, as St Catherine did all her life.
2027-04-29.question: Do I live my faith as a set of rules to carry, or as a love to abide in?
kidsaint: Catherine grew up in a big family in Siena, Italy; she had more than twenty brothers and sisters! She loved Jesus so much that she spent hours praying, and then went out to look after the sick and the poor. She was not afraid to talk even to the Pope and tell him what God wanted. Lesson: love Jesus with all your heart and speak the truth kindly and bravely.

family.explain: The first Christians decided together that everyone, from every country, is saved by the love and grace of Jesus, not by keeping a long list of rules. Jesus says: I love you as my Father loves me. Stay in my love, and you will have my joy. St Catherine stayed so close to Jesus that her joy and love were like a fire.
family.intention: We pray for the Pope, for Italy and Europe, and for everyone who works to make peace.
family.ask: Ask: “What makes us feel that Jesus loves us?”

illus: In 1376 Catherine, a dyer's daughter from Siena, travelled to Avignon in France, where the popes had lived for nearly seventy years. She had already written to Pope Gregory XI, calling him her sweet Christ on earth and begging him with great respect and great boldness to come back to Rome. Many cardinals opposed it. In January 1377 the Pope entered Rome. A young woman with no title or office had spoken truth to the highest authority on earth, not out of pride, but out of love for the Church.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you love us as the Father loves you. Keep us in your love and fill us with your joy. Amen.
share: We believe that we will be saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, just as they will (Acts 15:11). Do I try to earn God's love?
We should not trouble those Gentiles who are turning to God (Acts 15:19). Do I put unnecessary burdens on others who are coming to faith?
So that my joy may be in you, and that your joy may be complete (John 15:11). What steals my joy, and how can I abide in his love?
pm.resp: Proclaim his marvellous deeds to all the nations.
interc: For the Pope, that he may be strengthened by the prayers of the faithful as St Catherine strengthened the popes of her day.
For the unity of the Church, and for all who work to heal divisions.
For Italy and Europe, under the patronage of St Catherine, that they may rediscover their Christian roots.
For women who serve the Church with wisdom and courage, and for all lay Dominicans.
For our group, that we may abide in the love of Jesus and share his joy.
pm.close: Father, you made St Catherine burn with love for your Son and his Church. Through her prayers, keep us in his love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, after a long debate in Jerusalem, Peter stands up. He has seen the Holy Spirit fall on the Gentiles in the house of Cornelius. God made no distinction between them and us, he says, cleansing their hearts by faith. And then: we believe that we will be saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, just as they will (Acts 15:9–11). James confirms it, and the Church opens its doors wide.

Grace means gift. We do not earn God's love by a list of achievements, customs or good works. We receive it, and then our good works flow from it like fruit. The first Christians had to learn this together, and we have to learn it again every day.

Jesus tells us where that grace comes from: as the Father has loved me, so I have loved you; abide in my love (John 15:9). The love between the Father and the Son is offered to us. His commandments are not a heavy yoke; they are the walls of the house in which we abide in his love. And the purpose is joy: so that my joy may be in you, and that your joy may be complete (John 15:11).

St Catherine of Siena lived in that love. A dyer's daughter with little schooling, she prayed for hours, nursed plague victims, made peace between enemies, and spoke the truth even to the Pope, out of love for the Church. She told her friends (in substance) that if they were what they ought to be, they would set Italy on fire. Let us ask her to pray that we may abide in Christ's love, and let that fire spread. Amen.
kids: Children, St Catherine had more than twenty brothers and sisters! When she was small she loved to pray and to tell Jesus everything. When she grew up she looked after sick people when no one else would, and she even wrote letters to the Pope. Jesus says: I love you as my Father loves me; stay in my love. When we stay close to Jesus, we are full of joy, like Catherine!

intro: Salvation by the grace of the Lord Jesus, the Father's love poured out on us, and the fire of St Catherine of Siena.

sub: No distinction between them and us.
A yoke no one could bear.
q: It was not because you were more numerous than any other people that the Lord set his heart on you and chose you—for you were the fewest of all peoples. It was because the Lord loved you and kept the oath that he swore to your ancestors,
For by grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God
points.apply: Stop trying to earn God's love this week: begin each prayer with thanks for what you have received.

sub: As the Father has loved me.
Commandments as the walls of a home.
q: I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have continued my faithfulness to you.
As the Father has loved me, so I have loved you; abide in my love.
points.apply: Choose one commandment you find hard and keep it this week as a way of staying in his love, not as a rule.

sub: Truth spoken to the Pope in love.
q: for love is strong as death, passion fierce as the grave. Its flashes are flashes of fire, a raging flame. Many waters cannot quench love, neither can floods drown it.
“I came to bring fire to the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled!”
points.apply: Pray each day this week for the Pope and for one person who has drifted from the Church.

concl: The Church learned at Jerusalem that we are all saved by grace.
That grace is the Father's love for the Son poured into us; St Catherine shows what happens when a heart abides in it: joy, truth and fire.
2027-04-29.resolve: Read a few lines of St Catherine's prayers or letters this week and pray for the Church.
